messages:
rachael: heads up — saw a small cluster of reconnect spikes from eu-west around 1733332000. clients hit a short 'deadzone' and bounce twice before stabilizing. not a full outage but noisy.

kyle: can you paste the console link? want to check per-proxy breakdown.

rachael: https://console/redwood/streams?filter=region:eu-west,metric:reconnect_rate — look for the small hump starting ~1733331800.

sam: is this the same deadzone we tuned last quarter? the one that suppresses immediate reconnects for 20s?

maria: yep. current policy: reconnect_threshold=20s, deadzone_hold=15s. I suspect proxy-a has slightly higher egress latency so the client sees the socket as idle and retries earlier, hitting threshold repeatedly.

kyle: quick thought — rather than bumping threshold globally (affects latency-sensitive apps), can we annotate these events with deadzone_reason and sample them in telemetry? then dashboard can show impact before a global policy change.

rachael: agreed. patch idea: add tag deadzone=proxy-edge-a and deadzone_policy=soft to reconnect metrics when the server-side holds the socket open for <60s after idle.

sam: billing concern — we must ensure we don't double-charge token streams on reconnects. if we add tags only to metrics (no change to billing path) ok. but if we change routing fallback to re-establish sessions, it could trigger duplicate accounting.

maria: yes, keep billing path unchanged. plan: (1) add telemetry tags in runtime, (2) create dashboard panel that filters by deadzone=*, (3) run a 10% canary with tag-enabled, not policy change.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started: feat/deadzone-metrics-tags @ 1733333400 — targets: 10% of routing by proxy-a, duration: 30m.

devx: dashboard query to add — example for Console metrics query: `rate(reconnect_total{deadzone!=""}[5m])` and a panel grouping by `deadzone_policy` and `proxy`.

rachael: I'll open the PR with runtime tag + small e2e to ensure metrics emitted. I'll also add an annotation event in console when canary starts.

kyle: after canary, if we see >3x reconnects from same clients within 60s, we can consider a targeted policy tweak (eg. increase reconnect_threshold to 45s for proxy-a only). but prefer telemetry first.

sam: fine. also add an alert: if deadzone-tagged reconnect_rate > 50rps for 5m, paging to oncall with `ops:investigate` — so we don't miss escalations during canary.

rachael: noted. PR coming in ~15m. thanks all :thumbsup:
